subject: environmental-science

moments.title: Charles Moore finds the patch
moments.who: Charles Moore, Algalita Marine Research Foundation
moments.body: Moore, sailing through the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre after a yacht race, encounters extensive plastic debris in what becomes known as the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. His subsequent research (with Captain Curtis Ebbesmeyer) brings the concept of ocean plastic to public attention.
moments.takeaway: A subtropical ocean gyre had been concentrating plastic for decades before the wider public learned about it from one sailor's observation.

moments.title: Plastic found in Mariana Trench
moments.body: On a 10,927m dive into the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep), Vescovo's submersible records video of a plastic bag and sweet wrappers at the deepest point of the ocean.
moments.takeaway: There is no part of the ocean unaffected by human plastic. The lowest point of the seabed is contaminated.

now.title: Ocean plastics today
now.body: ~14 million tonnes of plastic enter the oceans annually. Microplastics are found in clouds, rain, breast milk and the placenta. The UN Global Plastics Treaty has been negotiated since 2022 (INC sessions 1-5). The Ocean Cleanup, single-use plastic bans and producer responsibility schemes attempt different scales of response.
now.open_questions: Can ocean cleanup work at scale? Most experts argue prevention upstream is far more effective than removal downstream.

reflection: Plastics were marketed in the 1950s as miracles. Disposable culture was an industry creation, not a consumer demand. The history of waste is the history of a manufactured behaviour.
